note: Recast from the revision by Constantino (1995), the original in English. The alate, the soldier and the large worker are described; the original marks the species as new (new species). Soldier measurements: 4 soldiers from 4 colonies, head length 5.90—6.80 mm, maximum head width 5.70—6.30 mm, head height without the postmentum 3.30—3.40 mm, frontal tube length 0.15—0.22 mm, left mandible length 3.80—4.10 mm, curvature 0.80—1.00 mm. Broken OCR numbers ("5. 90-6. .SO", ".3.30-.3.40") have been corrected from context.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is very similar to S. spinosus, but the latter has an antenna of only 20 segments. The soldier is very distinctive: head short, posterior margin distinctly trilobed, mandibles very long with degenerate marginal teeth, thoracic spines well developed, hind legs relatively long. The distribution appears to be limited to a small area of the western Amazon.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Eyes small, less than 1/4 of the head width; ocelli small; fontanelle round and medium-sized. Antenna 21 segments. Anterior corners of the pronotum angled and with a sharp point; lateral margins slightly S-shaped. Wings long; the ends of the media and cubitus distinct. Head capsule with a few scattered hairs; postclypeus with 6—8 hairs; outer margin of the pronotum hairy.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule short, head length and width subequal, the sides narrowing forwards; posterior margin of the head distinctly trilobed. Frontal tube prominent, the opening not visible in dorsal view. Labrum short and distinctly trilobed; lateral corners of the labrum acute; midlobe not elongate. Antenna 20—21 segments. Postmentum relatively short.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Large worker: head capsule large, with scattered erect hairs; fontanelle round and small. Antenna 20—21 segments. Mandibles similar to those of S. dirus, the molar plate rather narrow, the basal notch slightly more than 90°. Hindgut (dissected in the soldier) similar to that of S. dirus, but the elongate part of the midgut in the mixed segment relatively larger and the minor elongate part more slender.
